belief: I must have the latest things to be happy.
origins: Advertising, influencers, and peers keep telling us that the next phone, car, outfit, or gadget will fill the gap. The excitement of a new purchase is real and short-lived, and then the desire resets. Debt and clutter can follow.
teaches: Paul writes, “Godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into the world, so we cannot carry anything out of it. But if we have food and clothing, we will be content with these.” Jesus said, “Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.” Solomon wrote, “He who loves money is never satisfied by money.” The writer of Hebrews says, “Keep your lives free from the love of money and be content with what you have,” because God has promised never to leave or forsake us. Lasting joy comes from the Giver, not the gadget.
self_statements: I will be happy once I get that.
Everyone else has the new version.
Without it I am falling behind.
The next purchase will satisfy me.
errors: Believing a purchase will change how I feel for good.
Measuring myself by what others own.
Insisting that I should have the latest.
Feeling a want and treating it as a need.
questions: How long did happiness last after my last big purchase?
What emptiness am I hoping something will fill?
What do I already have that I once longed for?
How is my spending affecting my finances and peace?
What does Scripture say about contentment?
What would a 30-day pause before buying look like?
truth: Things cannot fill what only God can. Contentment is a learned gift that frees me from the treadmill. I can enjoy good things without needing the newest.
hw_truths: Godliness with contentment is great gain.
Life is not the abundance of possessions.
I already have what I once wanted.
log: Each week, name one thing that is enough and one purchase you paused.
actions: Write the last three purchases and how long the happiness lasted.
Donate something you no longer need.
Thank God for one old possession each day.
prayer: Lord, I chase the next thing. Teach me contentment, free me from the treadmill, and help me enjoy what I have and share it. Amen.
name_example: Sarah can write: “Godliness with contentment is great gain.”
